summary: Admit bounded approval-bound MAX message edit and delete through the existing Social API.

impacts.evidence: The existing tenant-scoped publication, channel account and remote receipt are the only source of the mutation target.
Released media is re-opened through the existing host boundary and provider responses are reduced to normalized results.
Existing provider-neutral Social edit/delete routes now admit MAX through additive runtime support without a new public endpoint.
No event envelope, event type or event payload changes.
MAX manifest and SDK adapter now implement the already defined SocialEditor and SocialDeleter interfaces.
Existing publication, remote receipt, operation receipt and audit storage are sufficient.
Approval, capability, exact configured channel, message ID validation and explicit provider success are required before mutation.
The existing social.publication.edit/delete approval and risk boundaries remain mandatory for MAX.
Existing operation and publication audit records preserve the immutable remote receipt and mutation outcome.
Tenant-scoped operation receipts prevent duplicate API calls; ambiguous writes are not retried.
Mutation egress is fixed to platform-api2.max.ru and released media uploads retain the existing exact host allowlist.
Existing MAX timeout, rate-limit and normalized write-outcome handling covers the new methods.
Removing the two runtime capabilities or registry branches closes MAX mutations without migration.
Deterministic adapter and registry tests verify exact methods, message ID, configured channel, success response and media upload path.
